plugins.name: mcpviews-gronk-speak
plugins.description: Optional MCPViews setup rules for terse nonpublic agent output style
plugins.author: MCPViews

manifest.name: mcpviews-gronk-speak
manifest.description: Optional MCPViews setup rules for terse nonpublic agent output style.

registry_index.summary: Optional Gronk Speak setup rules for compressed nonpublic agent output.

plugin_rules: Gronk Speak is an optional setup preference for terse nonpublic agent output. Use it only when the user has installed this plugin and persisted a non-off mode during MCPViews setup, or when the user explicitly asks for Gronk Speak.
Gronk Speak must never override user instructions, renderer payload requirements, safety, correctness, citations, warnings, commands, file paths, code, JSON, schema names, or test results.

Do not apply Gronk Speak by default to public-facing artifacts such as websites, emails, customer docs, PR descriptions/comments, published Ludflow docs, legal/medical/financial guidance, or user-facing copy.

setup_questions.question: Which Gronk Speak mode do you want for MCPViews setup-persisted agent output style?
setup_questions.description: Choose the compression level for allowed outputs. Gronk Speak is optional terse agent style: it cuts filler from setup/status chatter while preserving required facts, warnings, paths, commands, code, citations, and safety guardrails.
setup_questions.guidance: Explain that this controls only optional compression for agent-visible output within the selected scope. It is not required, it is not a public-copy style, and None is the safest default. Help the user choose by describing how natural or compressed each mode feels.

example_outputs.off: I will check the setup state, update the MCPViews rules if needed, and then ask the remaining setup preferences.
example_outputs.lite: Checking setup state, then updating only missing MCPViews rules.
example_outputs.full: Setup check -> patch missing MCPViews rules -> ask next preference.
example_outputs.ultra: Check setup -> patch rules -> ask next.

options.label: None
options.description: Best default. Use normal conversational assistant style unless the user explicitly asks for Gronk Speak.
options.persisted_rule: MCPViews Gronk Speak mode is off by default. Use normal assistant style unless the user explicitly asks for Gronk Speak.

options.label: Lite
options.description: Use shorter but still natural technical English for setup/status chatter; trims filler and repeated summaries.
options.persisted_rule: MCPViews Gronk Speak mode is lite. Where the selected Gronk scope allows it, use short direct technical English; cut filler, hedging, preambles, and repeated summaries while preserving required facts.

options.label: Full
options.description: Use compact internal-note style with fragments, fewer connective words, bullets, and -> for cause/effect.
options.persisted_rule: MCPViews Gronk Speak mode is full. Where the selected Gronk scope allows it, use compressed fragments, drop articles and connective fluff, prefer bullets, and use -> for cause/effect while preserving required facts.

options.label: Ultra
options.description: Use the least conversational mode: maximum compression with terse fragments and obvious abbreviations only when clarity survives.
options.persisted_rule: MCPViews Gronk Speak mode is ultra. Where the selected Gronk scope allows it, use maximum compression: terse fragments and obvious abbreviations only when clarity survives. Never sacrifice correctness or required facts.

setup_questions.question: Where should Gronk Speak apply when the mode is enabled?
setup_questions.description: Choose which nonpublic outputs may use Gronk compression. This scope is the safety boundary that keeps customer-facing or polished artifacts in normal prose unless the user explicitly asks otherwise.
setup_questions.guidance: Explain that scope decides where compression is allowed after a non-None mode is selected. Recommend Chat/status only for most users because it keeps durable docs and public-facing work polished.

options.label: Chat/status only
options.description: Best default. Apply only to assistant chat responses and progress updates.
options.persisted_rule: MCPViews Gronk Speak scope is chat_status_only. When Gronk Speak mode is enabled, apply it only to assistant chat responses and progress updates. Never apply by default to public-facing artifacts: websites, emails, customer docs, PR descriptions/comments, published Ludflow docs, legal/medical/financial guidance, or user-facing copy. Preserve commands, file paths, line refs, citations, error text, warnings, uncertainty, API names, schema fields, code, JSON, and test results. User style instructions, renderer payload requirements, safety, and correctness outrank compression. Do not promise hidden reasoning-token savings; Gronk Speak mainly targets visible output and persisted context size.

options.label: Internal artifacts
options.description: Apply to chat/status plus private plans, specs, incident notes, and research docs.
options.persisted_rule: MCPViews Gronk Speak scope is internal_artifacts. When Gronk Speak mode is enabled, apply it to assistant chat responses, progress updates, and private/internal plans, specs, incident notes, and research docs. Never apply by default to public-facing artifacts: websites, emails, customer docs, PR descriptions/comments, published Ludflow docs, legal/medical/financial guidance, or user-facing copy. Preserve commands, file paths, line refs, citations, error text, warnings, uncertainty, API names, schema fields, code, JSON, and test results. User style instructions, renderer payload requirements, safety, and correctness outrank compression. Do not promise hidden reasoning-token savings; Gronk Speak mainly targets visible output and persisted context size.

options.label: All nonpublic
options.description: Apply to any nonpublic output unless the user asks for polished prose.
options.persisted_rule: MCPViews Gronk Speak scope is all_nonpublic. When Gronk Speak mode is enabled, apply it to any nonpublic output unless the user asks for polished prose. Never apply by default to public-facing artifacts: websites, emails, customer docs, PR descriptions/comments, published Ludflow docs, legal/medical/financial guidance, or user-facing copy. Preserve commands, file paths, line refs, citations, error text, warnings, uncertainty, API names, schema fields, code, JSON, and test results. User style instructions, renderer payload requirements, safety, and correctness outrank compression. Do not promise hidden reasoning-token savings; Gronk Speak mainly targets visible output and persisted context size.

plugins.name: tribe-x-persona-studio
plugins.description: Consultant-scoped Persona Studio for creating TribeX AI personas and validating native MCPViews runs
plugins.author: TribeX AI

manifest.name: tribe-x-persona-studio

renderer_definitions.name: persona_lab
renderer_definitions.description: Standalone Persona Studio for editing consultant-scoped TribeX AI personas against the Cloudflare dev control plane and launching save-first single-run and parallel run batches.

registry_index.summary: Standalone consultant-scoped Persona Studio for editing TribeX AI personas through the Cloudflare dev control plane and launching native MCPViews single-run and parallel run test chats.

tool_groups.name: Relay Tests
tool_groups.hint: Deterministic local probe for verifying that Persona Studio grants can call MCPViews plugin tools through the desktop relay.

tool_rules.relay-probe: Use only for Persona Studio and MCPViews relay integration tests. Pass a unique marker and ask the tool to echo it back so the operator can verify the plugin relay path.

plugin_rules: Persona Studio is a standalone consultant-only authoring renderer that targets the TribeX AI Cloudflare dev control plane at https://dev.app.tribexai.com through MCPViews first-party AI configuration. It reads the currently selected native AI organization, requires that organization to have kind CONSULTANT, scopes every Persona Studio authoring call to that consultant organization, and launches save-first native AI single-run and parallel run batches in that organization.
Persona Studio is for creating and editing consultant-owned personas. Child organization assignment and enablement management remain outside this renderer in consultant/customer management flows.

The relay-probe tool is a local deterministic MCP tool for end-to-end testing of consultant-owned plugin relay grants. It requires tools/relay-probe-server.mjs to be running on http://127.0.0.1:4877/mcp.

plugins.name: email-deliverability
plugins.description: Visual email template drafting plus manual file-backed campaign launching with deterministic JSON/CSV audience filtering, derived filtered audience files, and platform-owned campaign workflow calls.
plugins.author: TribeX AI

manifest.name: email-deliverability

renderer_definitions.name: email_template_builder
renderer_definitions.description: Visual email template builder with guided org/workspace discovery, saved template selection, deterministic HTML-to-text preview, block selection in the HTML preview, durable workspace file search/load, and TribeX workspace JSON persistence.
renderer_definitions.rule: Use `email_template_builder` when the user wants to draft or edit a reusable HTML email template, choose a TribeX organization/workspace, select a saved durable template or create a new one, inspect explicit `{{variable}}` placeholders, preview HTML and derived plain text against a sample row, visually select rendered HTML blocks for persona-mediated edits, save the draft to TribeX AI workspace storage, or inspect advanced file/campaign fields only when needed.

renderer_definitions.name: email_campaign_launcher
renderer_definitions.description: Standalone manual campaign launcher for file-backed templates and JSON/CSV audiences, deterministic column filtering, filtered audience file creation, and direct platform-owned prepare, preview, test, review, apply, and status workflow calls.
renderer_definitions.rule: Use `email_campaign_launcher` when the user wants to manually trigger an approval-gated bulk email campaign from durable template and audience files, apply deterministic include/exclude filters over JSON paths or CSV headers, optionally save a renamed filtered derived audience file, and call the TribeX platform campaign workflow directly without composing a persona prompt.

renderer_definitions.name: email_campaign_history
renderer_definitions.description: Standalone campaign history dashboard for database-backed email campaign delivery stats, opens, opt-outs, link clicks, bounces, send times, and status refresh.
renderer_definitions.rule: Use `email_campaign_history` when the user wants to inspect sent or drafted campaign history, delivery stats, opens, opt-outs, link clicks, bounces, send times, status trends, or refresh campaign analytics from the platform database.

registry_index.summary: Visual email template drafting plus manual file-backed campaign launching with deterministic JSON/CSV audience filtering, derived filtered audience files, and platform-owned campaign workflow calls.

tool_groups.name: Template Builder
tool_groups.hint: Open, select organization/workspace, choose saved templates or create a new draft, validate variables, preview HTML plus deterministic plain text, and save deterministic template drafts for TribeX AI workspace storage.

tool_groups.name: Campaign Launcher
tool_groups.hint: Open the manual launcher, select saved template and audience files, apply deterministic JSON/CSV column filters, save a filtered audience file, and call platform campaign prepare, preview, test send, review, apply, and status without persona prompts.

tool_groups.name: Campaign History
tool_groups.hint: Open database-backed campaign history with delivery stats, opens, opt-outs, link clicks, bounces, send times, and status refresh.

tool_rules.email-template-builder-open: Returns a lightweight payload for the `email_template_builder` renderer. Use `push_content` with tool_name `email_template_builder` and the returned data to open the UI.
tool_rules.email-campaign-launcher-open: Returns a lightweight payload for the `email_campaign_launcher` renderer. Use `push_content` with tool_name `email_campaign_launcher` and the returned data to open the manual campaign UI.
tool_rules.email-campaign-history-open: Returns a lightweight payload for the `email_campaign_history` renderer. Use `push_content` with tool_name `email_campaign_history` and the returned data to open campaign history.
tool_rules.email-template-payload-validate: Validates explicit `{{variable}}` placeholders against normalized JSON audience rows. Missing variables block persona test prompt generation.
tool_rules.email-template-persona-test-prompt: Builds a safety-scoped prompt for a TribeX AI persona to call `email_campaign_prepare`, `email_campaign_preview`, and `email_campaign_test_send` for exactly one test recipient.
tool_rules.email-campaign-persona-prompt: Builds an approval-gated prompt for a TribeX AI persona to call prepare, preview, optional test send, MCPViews review proposal, send apply only after accepted approval, and status.
tool_rules.email-template-persona-revision-prompt: Builds a revision prompt for a TribeX AI persona to search for the selected HTML template file and update the same workspace path with an expected SHA-256 guard.
tool_rules.email-template-visual-edit-prompt: Builds a metadata-only batch visual-edit prompt for the plugin-specific `email-template-visual-editor` persona. The prompt uses selected rendered block metadata and requires same-path, SHA-guarded file updates.

plugin_rules: The email-deliverability plugin provides MCPViews template-building and manual campaign-launching UI. It does not send production email directly; all prepare, preview, test, review, apply, and status operations remain TribeX platform-owned.
The campaign builder consumes templates and audiences from workspace files, then creates database-backed drafted campaigns only when Prepare succeeds.

When a selected HTML template is being revised, pass its workspace path, file id, and SHA to the persona and prefer `email_template_search` plus `email_template_update`; do not create a new file for revisions unless the user explicitly asks for a copy.
Visual edits should use the plugin-specific `email-template-visual-editor` persona and metadata-only rendered block selections. Do not capture screenshots or store image files for visual edits in v1.
On open, the template builder should first guide the user through selecting a TribeX organization/workspace, then choosing a saved template or creating a new draft.

The default template editing view should stay simple: template name, key, subject, HTML source, variables, deterministic plain text preview, large HTML preview, and save. Campaign handoff fields belong behind advanced details or outside the template editor.

When opened with a workspace id or resolvable thread id, the campaign builder can search durable workspace storage under `email/`, filter by path, and load HTML template or audience files into the UI.
Template drafts may be saved as portable JSON files in TribeX AI durable workspace storage through `window.__tribexAiClient` when the renderer is opened with a workspace id or resolvable thread id.
The template builder's persona-fed campaign path must continue to use a TribeX AI persona with the platform email_campaign_* tools.

The manual `email_campaign_launcher` path must use renderer-accessible direct platform calls or a narrow platform broker, never a persona prompt. Prepare uses temporary inline filtered audience rows unless the user explicitly saves a renamed filtered JSON audience file under durable workspace storage. Saved files must preserve source file refs, hashes, filter specs, filter hashes, and count metadata. Sender configuration is resolved from organization web portal settings rather than manual launcher fields.

Scheduling from the manual campaign launcher UI is sufficient approval for production send apply; manual users never handle MCPViews review callbacks, approval tokens, object IDs, hashes, or storage paths in the default launcher flow.

The campaign history renderer is read-only and must load campaign analytics from platform-owned database history APIs, including send counts, opens, opt-outs, link clicks, bounces, and send timing metadata.

plugins.name: tribex-crm
plugins.description: Plugin-first interface and local MCP bridge for the lightweight TribeX CRM service.
plugins.author: TribeX AI

manifest.name: tribex-crm

renderer_definitions.name: tribex_crm
renderer_definitions.description: Standalone lightweight CRM workspace for accounts, contacts, opportunities, custom stages, and email audience handoff.
renderer_definitions.rule: Use `tribex_crm` when the user wants to browse or manage TribeX CRM records, inspect opportunities by stage, or prepare inline CRM audience rows for TribeX email workflows.

registry_index.summary: Plugin-first interface and local MCP bridge for the lightweight TribeX CRM service.

tool_groups.name: Records
tool_groups.hint: List, create, update, and archive CRM accounts, contacts, and opportunities.

tool_groups.name: Pipeline and Audience
tool_groups.hint: Manage pipeline stages and export normalized email audience rows.

tool_rules.tribex-crm-open: Returns a payload for the standalone `tribex_crm` renderer. Push the returned data to MCPViews with tool_name `tribex_crm`.
tool_rules.tribex-crm-audience-normalize: Normalizes CRM contact or audience-like rows into the email campaign audience shape with email/emailAddress/email_address.
tool_rules.export_audience: Returns normalized inline rows for email tools. Excludes archived and opted-out contacts by default.

plugin_rules: The TribeX CRM plugin is a lightweight operational workspace, not a marketing site.
CRM connection details are resolved by MCPViews and the local bridge; the renderer must not expose API, organization, user, or secret fields in the end-user UI.
The local bridge defaults to the deployed CRM service at https://crm.tribexai.com. Override TRIBEX_CRM_API_BASE only for local CRM service development.
Audience handoff returns inline rows only in v1; durable audience files are deferred until needed.
Production CRM persistence remains owned by the `tribex-crm` service; the plugin bridge must not invent a second storage layer.
